title: Control Plane Logbook: Routing/Auth/Quotas Pulse - 2026-11-18
content:
Overview:
Quick logbook from the control-plane weekly pulse focusing on routing tiering, auth token rotation, and quota enforcement heuristics. Notes taken during the call and immediately after — rough, action-oriented, and intended to seed follow-ups and tickets.

Attendees:
- Priya Singh (owner)
- Ethan Park (routing)
- Maya Alvarez (auth)
- Lukas Müller (quotas)
- Jana Ro (SRE)
- attendees joined late: Noor, Isaac

Context / Why this meeting:
- Routing experiments (multi-variant fallback) are entering canary next week; we need clear guardrails and rollback triggers.
- Auth team is preparing token rotation across Dedicated clusters and wants to surface any control-plane dependencies.
- Quotas engine is intermittently rejecting legitimate bursty flows for some dedicated customers; need telemetry and a hypothesis to test.

Highlights / Decisions:
1) Canary gating for routing fallback: agreed to add two additional SLO checks before widening canary: 95th p99 latency delta < 15% and error-rate spike < 0.5% absolute. If either fails for 15 minutes, auto-fallback to primary routing path. (Owner: Ethan)
2) Short-term auth mitigation: postpone global key rotation for Dedicated tenants with >24h request patterns until rotation helper tracks active KV cache sessions. Rollout will include a warm-up phase for session replication. (Owner: Maya)
3) Quotas soft-threshold behavior: switch back to soft-deny windows for customers flagged as "burst-prone" for 48 hours while we collect per-route histograms. This avoids repeated false rejects. (Owner: Lukas)

Action items (with next steps):
- Ethan: add the two SLO gating checks to the routing-canary pipeline and create a synthetic test that simulates model failover + traffic spike. Ticket: INF-3490. Due: 2026-11-22.
- Maya: implement a small helper service (auth-session-proxy) to emit active KV cache IDs to control-plane for rotation coordination; spike a PoC in the dev cluster. PR draft by 2026-11-21 (GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6794).
- Lukas: run a telemetry job to collect per-customer per-route burst histograms for the last 7 days, add sampling for header-based client-id. Share CSV by 2026-11-20.
- Jana (SRE): wire a pager path for the routing canary SLOs; add runbook snippet to Confluence section "Control Plane Canary Ops".
- Priya: consolidate these changes into a single control-plane release note and coordinate the Thursday release window; draft in confluence by 2026-11-20.

Open questions / Risks:
- Are there any downstream consumers of the auth key rotation events that depend on immediate invalidation? (Unclear — Maya to audit service list.)
- How will dedicated customers with heavy long-tail sessions react to the soft-deny window? Potential billing/UX questions for CS. Need a CS briefing if we change behavior beyond 72 hours.
- Routing canary synthetic test needs coverage for KV-cache warm starts — currently coverage missing for cross-node prefix cache warmup.

Incidents & Recent Signals:
- Nov 16th: one Dedicated customer (cust-331) saw quota rejects for a short period (~12 minutes) during a regional deploy. Root cause: quota evaluation race when the customer sent two near-simultaneous big-batch requests and burst detection misclassified the flow. Logs attached to INF-3467.
- Latency: p50 stable, p95 up 8% last 48h in us-west-2 for the primary routing path; investigation points to increased small-request fanout from a single partner integration.

Runbook edits proposed (quick sketch):
- Routing Canary: insert SLO-gated auto-fallback step; add an explicit checklist for cache warmup verification and synthetic-run pass criteria.
- Auth Rotation: add "skip-global-rotation" flag for Dedicated tenants with session-count > 10k and require warm-replication confirmation.
- Quotas: add a diagnostic endpoint /controlplane/quotas/debug that returns last-10-eval decisions and counts for a tenant (only callable by SRE/SE).

Notes to self / informal fragments:
- "experiment-id" header idea for routing tests — makes diffing logs across canary easier.
- Could we add a temporary per-tenant grace token to avoid hard denies on rotation days? (low-effort: header-based allowlist)
- Remember to ping CS about possible communication for cust-331 

Follow-up meeting schedule:
- Quick sync Fri 2026-11-20 09:00 PT (15m) to confirm gating metrics and PR readiness.
- Full platform retro Wed 2026-11-25 11:00 PT (30m) to assess the canary after week of testing.

Related tickets / links referenced during the discussion:
- INF-3421 (routing fallback design)
- INF-3467 (quota rejects incident)
- INF-3490 (routing canary SLO gating)
- GH PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6789, https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6794
- Confluence: Control Plane Runbook (see edits in "Canary Ops" section)

Attachment notes (where to find logs/graphs):
- SLO dashboards: dashboard id: "pltfm-routing-canary-v2" in Grafana (link in Confluence).
- Quotas histogram CSV export: will be uploaded to the shared folder: /shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/telemetry/quotas/

Closing thoughts:
- Consensus that we should be conservative on canary widening until the synthetic tests + gating prove stable.
- Auth rotation needs a small coordination shim, not a full rewrite — aim for incremental changes that can be reverted cleanly.
- Quotas telemetry looks like the highest-value near-term work to reduce false positives.

Status: draft notes; please add inline comments on Confluence or tag me in the ticket if you have objections or additional context.
